ai_sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS cancelled_shipments
FROM shipments
WHERE status = 'Cancelled'
  AND created_date >= '2026-07-01'
  AND created_date < '2026-10-01';
ai_answer: Last quarter, 946 shipments were cancelled. This counts shipments with a status of Cancelled that were created between July 1, 2026 and September 30, 2026.

question: What % of UK shipments were held at customs?
ai_sql:
SELECT 100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN s.hold_reason = 'At Customs' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) AS pct_held_at_customs
FROM shipments s
JOIN shippers sh ON s.shipper_id = sh.shipper_id
WHERE sh.country = 'UK';
ai_answer: About 8.2% of shipments from UK shippers were held at customs. This covers all UK shipments in the records, with no date restriction, and counts only shipments whose hold reason is "At Customs."

question: Compare on-time rate and cost per package for milkrun vs direct, last quarter.
ai_sql:
WITH q AS (
    SELECT run_id, run_type, cost_eur
    FROM truck_runs
    WHERE run_date >= '2026-07-01' AND run_date < '2026-10-01'
),
rp AS (
    SELECT run_id, SUM(packages) AS pkgs
    FROM shipments
    GROUP BY run_id
),
ot AS (
    SELECT q.run_type,
           SUM(CASE WHEN s.delivered_to_node_date <= s.promised_date THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS on_time,
           COUNT(*) AS delivered
    FROM shipments s
    JOIN q ON q.run_id = s.run_id
    WHERE s.status <> 'Cancelled'
      AND s.delivered_to_node_date IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY q.run_type
),
cost AS (
    SELECT q.run_type,
           SUM(q.cost_eur) AS total_cost,
           SUM(rp.pkgs) AS total_pkgs
    FROM q
    JOIN rp ON rp.run_id = q.run_id
    GROUP BY q.run_type
)
SELECT c.run_type,
       ROUND(1.0 * o.on_time / o.delivered, 4) AS on_time_rate,
       ROUND(c.total_cost / c.total_pkgs, 4) AS cost_per_package_eur
FROM cost c
JOIN ot o ON o.run_type = c.run_type;
ai_answer: Milkrun was cheaper per package but less punctual than direct. Direct runs delivered on time 94.45% of the time at €4.7737 per package, while milkrun runs delivered on time 78.09% of the time at €2.6363 per package. This covers truck runs dated 1 July to 30 September 2026, excluding cancelled shipments and shipments with no delivery date.

question: What was our weekly attainment for FR shippers last quarter?
ai_sql:
WITH fr AS (
    SELECT shipper_id FROM shippers WHERE country = 'FR'
),
act AS (
    SELECT strftime('%Y-%W', s.created_date) AS wk,
           SUM(s.packages) AS actual_packages
    FROM shipments s
    JOIN fr ON s.shipper_id = fr.shipper_id
    WHERE s.created_date >= '2026-07-01'
      AND s.created_date < '2026-10-01'
      AND s.status <> 'Cancelled'
    GROUP BY wk
),
fc AS (
    SELECT strftime('%Y-%W', f.forecast_date) AS wk,
           SUM(f.forecast_packages) AS forecast_packages
    FROM forecasts f
    JOIN fr ON f.shipper_id = fr.shipper_id
    WHERE f.forecast_date >= '2026-07-01'
      AND f.forecast_date < '2026-10-01'
    GROUP BY wk
)
SELECT fc.wk AS week,
       COALESCE(act.actual_packages, 0) AS actual_packages,
       fc.forecast_packages,
       ROUND(1.0 * COALESCE(act.actual_packages, 0) / fc.forecast_packages, 3) AS attainment
FROM fc
LEFT JOIN act ON act.wk = fc.wk
ORDER BY fc.wk;
ai_answer: Weekly attainment for French shippers last quarter (July 1 to September 30, 2026) ranged from 90.8% in week 39 to 99.6% in week 29, and it was below 100% in every week. Attainment is actual packages divided by forecast packages, and cancelled shipments were excluded from actuals. The first (week 26) and last (week 39) weeks only partly fall within the quarter, so they cover fewer days.

question: Which 10 shippers had the lowest attainment in Q3 2026?
ai_sql:
WITH f AS (
    SELECT shipper_id, SUM(forecast_packages) AS fc
    FROM forecasts
    WHERE forecast_date >= '2026-07-01' AND forecast_date <= '2026-09-30'
    GROUP BY shipper_id
),
s AS (
    SELECT shipper_id, SUM(packages) AS act
    FROM shipments
    WHERE created_date >= '2026-07-01' AND created_date <= '2026-09-30'
      AND status <> 'Cancelled'
    GROUP BY shipper_id
)
SELECT sh.shipper_id,
       sh.name,
       f.fc AS forecast_packages,
       COALESCE(s.act, 0) AS actual_packages,
       ROUND(1.0 * COALESCE(s.act, 0) / f.fc, 3) AS attainment
FROM f
JOIN shippers sh ON sh.shipper_id = f.shipper_id
LEFT JOIN s ON s.shipper_id = f.shipper_id
WHERE f.fc > 0
ORDER BY attainment ASC
LIMIT 10;
ai_answer: The 10 shippers with the lowest attainment in Q3 2026 (July 1 to September 30) are led by Bruneau 263 at 0.643 and Turner, Ford and Dobson 87 at 0.650, with Roy Toussaint et Fils 385 at 0.690 as the 10th-lowest. Attainment is actual packages shipped divided by forecast packages, so 0.643 means the shipper moved 0.643 of its forecast volume. Actuals exclude cancelled shipments, and only shippers with a positive forecast for the quarter are included.

question: Did any de-listed shipper have volume after being de-listed?
ai_sql:
SELECT s.shipper_id,
       s.name,
       s.delisted_date,
       COUNT(sh.shipment_id) AS shipments_after_delisting,
       SUM(sh.packages) AS packages_after_delisting,
       SUM(sh.pallets) AS pallets_after_delisting
FROM shippers s
JOIN shipments sh
  ON sh.shipper_id = s.shipper_id
 AND sh.created_date > s.delisted_date
WHERE s.status = 'de-listed'
GROUP BY s.shipper_id, s.name, s.delisted_date
ORDER BY shipments_after_delisting DESC;
ai_answer: No de-listed shipper had any shipments dated after their de-listing date. The check covered every shipper currently marked as de-listed and counted only shipments created after each shipper's de-listing date. Because nothing matched, there are no shipment, package, or pallet totals to report.

question: What was average truck utilisation by country last month?
ai_sql:
SELECT n.country,
       AVG(tr.pallets_loaded * 1.0 / NULLIF(tr.pallet_capacity, 0)) AS avg_utilisation
FROM truck_runs tr
JOIN nodes n ON n.node_id = tr.node_id
WHERE strftime('%Y-%m', tr.run_date) = strftime('%Y-%m', date('2026-10-19', 'start of month', '-1 day'))
GROUP BY n.country;
ai_answer: Across the four countries, average truck utilisation for September 2026 ranged from 0.639 in France to 0.647 in Spain, with Italy at 0.643 and the UK at 0.647. Utilisation here is pallets loaded divided by pallet capacity for each truck run, averaged within each country, so 1.0 would mean full. The figures cover truck runs dated 1 to 30 September 2026, and the query treats September as "last month" based on a fixed reference date of 19 October 2026.

question: Which nodes went over capacity during peak 2025, and on how many days?
ai_sql:
-- Assumes "peak 2025" = Oct-Dec 2025 and measures daily load as pallets delivered to each node.
WITH daily AS (
    SELECT s.node_id,
           date(s.delivered_to_node_date) AS d,
           SUM(s.pallets) AS pallets
    FROM shipments s
    WHERE s.node_id IS NOT NULL
      AND s.delivered_to_node_date IS NOT NULL
      AND date(s.delivered_to_node_date) >= '2025-10-01'
      AND date(s.delivered_to_node_date) < '2026-01-01'
    GROUP BY s.node_id, date(s.delivered_to_node_date)
)
SELECT n.node_id,
       n.city,
       n.country,
       n.daily_capacity_pallets,
       COUNT(*) AS days_over_capacity
FROM daily d
JOIN nodes n ON n.node_id = d.node_id
WHERE d.pallets > n.daily_capacity_pallets
GROUP BY n.node_id, n.city, n.country, n.daily_capacity_pallets
ORDER BY days_over_capacity DESC;
ai_answer: Only one node went over its daily capacity during peak 2025: the London, UK node (N-UK-01), which exceeded its limit of 150 pallets on 6 days. This covers October through December 2025 and counts pallets delivered to each node per day.

question: Which Account Managers' shippers drove the most avoidable cost last quarter?
ai_sql:
WITH wasted_runs AS (
  SELECT run_id, cost_eur
  FROM truck_runs
  WHERE run_outcome = 'wasted'
    AND run_date >= '2026-07-01'
    AND run_date < '2026-10-01'
),
run_shippers AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT rs.run_id, rs.shipper_id
  FROM run_stops rs
  JOIN wasted_runs w ON w.run_id = rs.run_id
),
allocated AS (
  SELECT rsh.run_id,
         rsh.shipper_id,
         w.cost_eur * 1.0 / COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY rsh.run_id) AS cost_share
  FROM run_shippers rsh
  JOIN wasted_runs w ON w.run_id = rsh.run_id
)
SELECT s.account_manager,
       ROUND(SUM(a.cost_share), 2) AS avoidable_cost_eur,
       COUNT(DISTINCT a.run_id) AS wasted_runs
FROM allocated a
JOIN shippers s ON s.shipper_id = a.shipper_id
GROUP BY s.account_manager
ORDER BY avoidable_cost_eur DESC;
ai_answer: Denis Davies's shippers drove the most avoidable cost last quarter, at €20,812.38 across 73 wasted truck runs. Alphonse Durand (€18,349.37 across 71 runs) and Angelica Santi (€16,714.38 across 61 runs) came next. The figures cover runs from 1 July to 30 September 2026 that were marked as wasted, and each run's cost is split evenly among the shippers on that run.

question: How much unplanned volume did we get on bank holidays in 2026, by country?
ai_sql:
SELECT n.country,
       SUM(t.pallets_loaded) AS unplanned_pallets,
       COUNT(*) AS adhoc_runs
FROM truck_runs t
JOIN nodes n ON t.node_id = n.node_id
JOIN holidays h ON h.country = n.country AND h.holiday_date = t.run_date
WHERE t.is_adhoc = 1
  AND strftime('%Y', t.run_date) = '2026'
GROUP BY n.country;
ai_answer: In 2026, unplanned (ad hoc) truck runs that fell on a bank holiday moved 79 pallets in Spain, 136 in France, 92 in Italy, and 119 in the UK. Those runs were 46, 82, 54, and 67 in number, respectively. Only runs dated on a holiday in the same country as the node are counted.

question: Which shippers missed the +/-10% attainment band for 3+ consecutive weeks?
ai_sql:
WITH fw AS (
    SELECT shipper_id,
           date(forecast_date, '-' || ((CAST(strftime('%w', forecast_date) AS INTEGER) + 6) % 7) || ' days') AS wk,
           SUM(forecast_packages) AS fc
    FROM forecasts
    GROUP BY shipper_id, wk
),
aw AS (
    SELECT shipper_id,
           date(created_date, '-' || ((CAST(strftime('%w', created_date) AS INTEGER) + 6) % 7) || ' days') AS wk,
           SUM(packages) AS act
    FROM shipments
    WHERE status <> 'Cancelled'
    GROUP BY shipper_id, wk
),
wk_att AS (
    SELECT f.shipper_id,
           f.wk,
           f.fc,
           COALESCE(a.act, 0) AS act,
           COALESCE(a.act, 0) * 1.0 / NULLIF(f.fc, 0) AS attainment
    FROM fw f
    LEFT JOIN aw a ON a.shipper_id = f.shipper_id AND a.wk = f.wk
),
missed AS (
    SELECT shipper_id,
           wk,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY shipper_id ORDER BY wk) AS rn
    FROM wk_att
    WHERE attainment IS NULL
       OR attainment < 0.9
       OR attainment > 1.1
),
streaks AS (
    SELECT shipper_id,
           CAST(julianday(wk) AS INTEGER) - 7 * rn AS grp,
           COUNT(*) AS consecutive_missed_weeks
    FROM missed
    GROUP BY shipper_id, grp
)
SELECT s.shipper_id,
       sh.name,
       MAX(s.consecutive_missed_weeks) AS max_consecutive_missed_weeks
FROM streaks s
LEFT JOIN shippers sh ON sh.shipper_id = s.shipper_id
GROUP BY s.shipper_id, sh.name
HAVING MAX(s.consecutive_missed_weeks) >= 3
ORDER BY s.shipper_id;
ai_answer: **873 shippers** missed the ±10% attainment band for at least three consecutive weeks. This covers every week in the forecast data, with no date range applied. Cancelled shipments were excluded, and a week counts as missed if actual packages came in under 90% or over 110% of forecast, or if there was no forecast to compare against. In the first 50 shippers shown, the longest run is 92 consecutive weeks for Fisher Ltd, and Griffiths LLC has 19.
